title: Container Bookings: when a customer roll is accepted and when it is charged
content:
## Policy clause
Under the Container Bookings product line, a customer roll follows the customer's request for another sailing, or documents received after grace under the late documentation rules. A customer roll is accepted only while the booking's customer rolls recorded so far are fewer than the tier's customer roll limit. Beyond that the customer must cancel under the cancellation rules and book again.

A customer roll is free while the booking's customer rolls, counted including the roll being handled, do not exceed the tier's free customer rolls. Beyond the free allowance, the fee is written as a customer roll fee entry of the amendment-fee kind, marked as a customer-requested vessel change.

## Acceptance and fee truth table (hypothetical tier)
*Hypothetical tier with 1 free customer roll and a limit of 3, for illustration only:*
| Customer rolls recorded before this one | Accepted? | Count including this roll | Fee? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | yes | 1 | free |
| 1 | yes | 2 | charged |
| 2 | yes | 3 | charged |
| 3 | no; cancel and book again | not applicable | not applicable |

## Points of judgement
**Is the free allowance checked before or after counting the current roll?** After: the roll being handled is included in the count that is compared with the free allowance.

**Is the limit checked the same way?** No. The limit compares the customer rolls recorded so far, before this roll, and they must be fewer than the limit.

**The customer's SI arrived after grace and the booking was moved. Is that a customer roll?** Yes. Documents received after grace lead to a customer roll.

## Retired wording
The former statement that a customer roll beyond the free allowance is charged the per-container customer roll fee multiplied by the container count is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the customer roll fee.

superseded_clauses: is otherwise charged customer_roll_fee_per_container_usd times the container_count
